title: What is a White Card, and how do you get one in NSW?
summary: You need a White Card to work on a construction site. Here's how to get one in NSW and how long it stays valid.
body:
A White Card (general construction induction card) is required for anyone who carries out construction work, including labourers, tradespeople and site supervisors. Most of our labouring roles need one.

How to get one in NSW

  1. Book a course in general construction induction training with a Registered Training Organisation (RTO) approved by SafeWork NSW. The course is CPCWHS1001 Prepare to work safely in the construction industry.
  2. Bring 100 points of identification to your trainer.
  3. Complete the training. Your trainer gives you a statement of training you can use for 60 days while your card arrives from SafeWork NSW.

You can also add a digital White Card to the Service NSW app, but you still need to carry the physical card.

Does it expire?

Your White Card becomes void if you haven't done construction work for two years in a row. NSW recognises White Cards issued in other states and territories.

Official information: SafeWork NSW: White cards.
